title: Cell delta elevated during charge
description: One cell group is more than 30 mV from the pack median while charging.
likely_causes: Uneven cell aging; balancer duty cycle too low; loose sense lead
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Compare group voltages in the BMS snapshot. 2) Confirm the balancer is running. 3) Reseat the sense harness if the delta is on one channel only.

title: Charge complete
description: The pack reached the configured SOC maximum and charge current tapered to standby.
likely_causes: Normal end of charge
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Confirm SOC matches the coulomb count. 2) No field action if the taper was controlled.

title: SOC residual above estimate band
description: The SOC estimator and the coulomb counter differ by more than 8 points.
likely_causes: Current sensor offset; estimator bias after a partial cycle; stale voltage reference
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Rest the pack for 20 minutes and compare open-circuit voltage to SOC. 2) Check current-sensor zero. 3) Do not recalibrate until the residual repeats.

title: Charge rate limited by temperature
description: The BMS reduced charge current because pack temperature entered the derate band.
likely_causes: High ambient; cooling airflow low; sustained charge
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Read pack temperature and the cooling command. 2) Confirm inlet air path. 3) Compare with the site sensor.

title: Cell group voltage imbalance
description: A cell group diverged by more than 80 mV under discharge above 70 kW.
likely_causes: HW-C power-module busbar torque below spec; cell group connection resistance; voltage sense drift
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Capture group voltages at the next discharge above 70 kW. 2) Compare hardware revision. 3) Torque-check the HW-C busbar before replacing cells.

title: Charge current above setpoint
description: Charge current exceeded the configured max for one sample and then returned.
likely_causes: Transient setpoint overshoot; current sensor spike; charger handshake glitch
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Check whether the spike lasted more than one sample. 2) Compare current sensor to the inverter DC reading. 3) Clear if it does not repeat.

title: Unexpected SOC step
description: Reported SOC changed by more than 25 points without a matching charge or discharge energy.
likely_causes: Unconfirmed: SOC estimator bias; current-sensor offset; unmetered standby load
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Compare SOC to integrated current across the step. 2) Check firmware against peers. 3) Do not declare a cause until a second instrument agrees.

title: Contactor opened under load
description: The main contactor opened while discharge current was above 20 A.
likely_causes: Contactor coil driver fault; precharge circuit open; protection latch
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Read the contactor coil current at the trip. 2) Check precharge voltage rise time. 3) Leave the pack open until the driver or precharge part is identified.

title: Cell balancing active
description: The BMS enabled passive balancing on one or more cell groups.
likely_causes: Normal balancing after a charge
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Confirm balance current is inside the BMS spec. 2) No action if group delta is falling.

title: BMS temperature channels disagree
description: Two BMS temperature channels differ by more than 6 C while current is below 10 A.
likely_causes: Sensor drift; harness resistance; real local hotspot
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Compare both channels to the pack current. 2) A drift case stays high at zero current. 3) A hotspot rises with current.

title: BMS watchdog restart
description: The BMS watchdog reset the controller and the pack returned to the previous state within one minute.
likely_causes: Supply dip; firmware task overrun; noise on the reset line
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Count restarts in 24 hours. 2) Check the 12 V rail. 3) Escalate if more than three restarts occur in a day.

title: Cell voltage sense channel stale
description: A voltage sense channel missed three updates.
likely_causes: Sense harness; BMS analog front end; connector fretting
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Identify the stale channel. 2) Swap the sense lead to a known-good port if the procedure allows. 3) Replace the harness before the BMS board.

title: BMS safety latch
description: The BMS latched a safety output and opened the contactors.
likely_causes: Real protection event; failed safety input; firmware latch bug
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Read the latch source bit. 2) Do not clear the latch until telemetry around the bit is saved.

title: Inverter online
description: The inverter completed precharge and closed its AC contactor.
likely_causes: Normal start
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Confirm grid voltage and frequency are inside limits. 2) No action.

title: Inverter protection latch
description: The inverter latched offline after a protection comparison failed.
likely_causes: Grid excursion; hardware trip; nuisance comparison after a firmware change
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Read the latch reason. 2) Compare grid frequency and voltage in the minute before the latch. 3) Leave the latch set if the grid trace is still outside limits.

title: Inverter thermal derate
description: AC output was reduced because the inverter heat sink crossed the derate threshold.
likely_causes: Blocked airflow; high ambient; fan wear
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Compare heat-sink temperature to power. 2) Inspect the inverter fan. 3) Derate is expected only above the configured temperature threshold.

title: Restart delay active
description: The inverter is waiting out the configured restart delay before reconnecting.
likely_causes: Recent trip; configured delay; operator command
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Read the delay timer. 2) Confirm the delay matches the approved configuration.

title: DC bus ripple above spec
description: DC bus ripple exceeded 25 V peak to peak at power above 40 kW.
likely_causes: DC bus capacitor ESR rise; loose DC link; current sensor noise
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Capture ripple at a known power. 2) Compare with a sister inverter on the same bus. 3) Plan a power-module swap if ESR is high on HW-B modules.

title: AC overvoltage ride-through
description: Grid voltage entered the ride-through band and the inverter stayed online.
likely_causes: Utility switching; tap changer; local capacitor switching
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Record the voltage peak and duration. 2) No inverter repair if the event stayed inside the ride-through curve.

title: Output capped below commanded power
description: Commanded discharge was above the measured AC power by more than 10 kW for at least 15 minutes.
likely_causes: Inverter power limit set below the engineered value; thermal derate; current limit
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Read Inverter Power Limit and compare it to the expected value. 2) Check configuration_status. 3) Confirm temperature is not in derate.

title: Inverter output collapsed
description: AC power fell by more than 50 kW in one sample while the grid was inside normal limits.
likely_causes: Phase module fault; gate-driver undervoltage; DC input sag
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Compare grid voltage and DC bus at the drop. 2) If the grid is normal and the bus sags, inspect the power module. 3) Open a hardware ticket if the output stays down.

title: Inverter hardware trip
description: A hardware comparator tripped the inverter faster than the software loop.
likely_causes: Desaturation; overcurrent; failed gate driver
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Do not restart more than once. 2) Capture the hardware trip code. 3) Replace the power module if desaturation is set.

title: Link quality nominal
description: Heartbeat latency and signal strength are inside the nominal band.
likely_causes: Normal operation
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) No action.

title: Gateway link loss
description: The gateway stopped acknowledging heartbeats after signal strength fell and latency rose.
likely_causes: Antenna or cable; interference; failed gateway radio
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Compare latency and signal strength. 2) A radio fault moves both. 3) A firmware heartbeat fault moves latency only. 4) Inspect the antenna if signal strength fell by more than 15 dBm.

title: Intermittent telemetry gap
description: More than two expected telemetry frames were missing in 30 minutes.
likely_causes: Latency rise; retransmission; gateway buffer
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Check communication latency and signal strength. 2) Count gaps before escalating.

title: Heartbeat session dropped
description: The session layer dropped a healthy link when one-way latency exceeded 120 ms. Signal strength stays nominal.
likely_causes: Firmware 4.3.0 heartbeat state machine regression
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Confirm signal strength is unchanged. 2) Confirm the device is on 4.3.0. 3) Roll back to 4.2.1 or upgrade to 4.3.1. 4) Do not replace the radio if signal strength is nominal.

title: Compressed telemetry frames enabled
description: The gateway is sending the compressed frame format introduced in 4.3.0.
likely_causes: Firmware feature
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Confirm the collector accepts compressed frames. 2) No fault action.

title: Pack temperature above warning threshold
description: Pack temperature crossed 48 C. This is a warning, not a shutdown.
likely_causes: Real heat rise; sensor drift; high ambient
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Compare the rate of rise. 2) A real rise tracks current and does not snap back. 3) A drifting sensor rises at low current and snaps back after replacement.

title: Temperature rate of change implausible
description: Reported temperature changed faster than the pack thermal mass allows.
likely_causes: Temperature sensor drift or a loose sensor lead
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Compare the step to pack current. 2) Check the redundant channel. 3) Replace the sensor if the channels disagree at low current.

title: Pack thermal protective shutdown
description: The BMS opened the contactors because pack temperature crossed the protective threshold.
likely_causes: Cooling fan stopped; blocked airflow; sustained discharge
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Read temperature for the two hours before the trip. 2) Confirm the cooling fan tach. 3) Do not raise the temperature threshold to clear this fault. 4) Replace the fan if tach is zero while temperature is rising.

title: Grid voltage outside preferred band
description: Grid voltage left the preferred band but stayed inside the trip limits.
likely_causes: Utility regulation; local switching
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Record duration. 2) Compare with the neighboring site. 3) No inverter repair for a shared grid dip.

title: Grid nominal
description: Grid voltage and frequency returned to the nominal band.
likely_causes: Normal recovery
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) No action.

title: Grid frequency excursion
description: Grid frequency left the 59.5 to 60.5 Hz operating band.
likely_causes: Utility disturbance; islanding; measurement error
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Confirm the excursion on the inverter and the gateway. 2) If both agree, treat it as a grid event. 3) The inverter may latch even after frequency returns.

title: Grid disconnect
description: The inverter opened the AC contactor because the grid stayed outside limits past the ride-through timer.
likely_causes: Sustained grid disturbance; failed grid relay
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Save the pre-trip waveform. 2) Reclose only after the grid is inside limits for the restart delay.

title: Signal strength declining
description: RSSI fell more than 8 dBm from the site baseline and is still falling.
likely_causes: Antenna alignment; foliage; interference; failing radio
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Compare RSSI to latency. 2) Inspect the antenna if latency is still low. 3) Escalate if RSSI crosses -95 dBm.

title: Gateway CPU elevated
description: Gateway CPU stayed above 80 percent for 10 minutes.
likely_causes: Firmware 4.4.0 lab build; log flood; retry storm
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Check the firmware version. 2) Confirm this is not a 4.3.0 heartbeat storm. 3) Capture a CPU profile before replacing hardware.

title: Gateway restart loop
description: The gateway rebooted more than three times in an hour.
likely_causes: Power supply; firmware crash; watchdog
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Read the reboot reason. 2) Check the supply rail. 3) Hold the device out of the firmware rollout if the reboot reason is a panic.

title: Firmware bank verified
description: The inactive firmware bank signature matched the release manifest.
likely_causes: Normal update pre-check
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) No action.

title: Heartbeat regression signature
description: The device logged the 4.3.0 heartbeat state-machine signature while the radio link was healthy.
likely_causes: Firmware 4.3.0 communications regression
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Confirm version 4.3.0. 2) Upgrade to 4.3.1 or roll back to 4.2.1. 3) Use COM-214 as the customer-facing fault code.

title: Power limit below rated power
description: Inverter Power Limit is more than 10 kW below the nameplate rating.
likely_causes: Configuration mismatch; intentional derate
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Compare parameter_value to expected_value. 2) If they differ, the row is a mismatch, not a hardware fault.

title: Configuration outside approved envelope
description: A running parameter does not match the approved expected value for the site.
likely_causes: Field edit without an engineering change; stale template
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Open device_configuration for the device. 2) Restore the expected value through a change record. 3) Confirm faults stop after the new last_modified time.

title: Contactor coil driver fault
description: The contactor was commanded closed and the coil current stayed at zero.
likely_causes: Failed coil driver; open coil; harness
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Measure coil current. 2) If the command is present and current is zero, replace the driver. 3) Do not confuse this with a precharge-resistor failure.

title: Precharge resistor open
description: DC bus voltage did not rise during the precharge window, so the main contactor stayed open.
likely_causes: Open precharge resistor; welded precharge relay; blown fuse
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Check precharge voltage slope. 2) A coil-driver fault still shows coil current at zero. 3) This fault shows coil current present and no voltage rise.

title: Redundant temperature channels diverged
description: The primary pack temperature and the redundant channel differ by more than 8 C.
likely_causes: Primary sensor drift; redundant sensor drift; real gradient
recommended_diagnostic_steps: 1) Trust the channel that agrees with current and with the site probe. 2) Replace the divergent sensor. 3) Do not shut the pack down on one divergent channel if current is low.
